overview: This bill expands the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, a National Park Service site around San Francisco Bay, to take in a piece of land called the Scarper Ridge property. It does this by adding the land, as shown on a July 2024 Park Service map, to the list of areas that make up the recreation area under the 1972 law that created it. Once inside the boundary, the land can be managed as part of the park. The bill is very short and makes no other changes. As of March 27, 2026, it had passed the Senate and was waiting at the House desk for action.
for: Supporters say bringing Scarper Ridge inside the park boundary lets the Park Service protect the open land and manage it alongside the surrounding parkland for public use.
against: Critics say every addition to a national park adds to the Park Service's long list of upkeep needs, and the bill does not say how the new land's care would be paid for.
